(men's basketball)|Beşiktaş Gain]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]] before starting his professional career in Europe, then moving to the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), and back to Europe again. ==Early life== Matt Thomas was born in [[Decatur, Illinois]]. He grew up in [[Onalaska, Wisconsin]], attending [[Onalaska High School (Wisconsin)|Onalaska High School]]. His mother had been a standout high school athlete herself. She was a swimmer, softball player, tennis player, and basketball star. She holds the school record for single game scoring at [[Wahlert Catholic High School|Wahlert High School]] in [[Dubuque, Iowa]], with 48 points.{{cite web |last1=Sommerfeldt |first1=Todd |title=Family tragedy and glory help shape Onalaska's Matt Thomas |url=http://lacrossetribune.com/sports/high-school/onalaskahilltoppers/family-tragedy-and-glory-help-shape-onalaska-s-matt-thomas/article_4d08785a-65bc-11e1-ada1-001871e3ce6c.html |website=La Crosse Tribune |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120312050113/http://lacrossetribune.com/sports/high-school/onalaskahilltoppers/family-tragedy-and-glory-help-shape-onalaska-s-matt-thomas/article_4d08785a-65bc-11e1-ada1-001871e3ce6c.html |archivedate=March 12, 2012 |date=March 4, 2012}} Thomas suffered tragedy at a young age. When he was 9 years old, his father, Greg, who suffered from alcoholism, died of suicide. Because of this, Thomas developed a very strong relationship with his mother.{{cite web |last1=Gottlieb |first1=Doug |title=Iowa State's 6th man and the struggle of grief, love and basketball |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/iowa-states-6th-man-and-the-struggle-of-grief-love-and-basketball/ |website=CBSSports.com |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=December 10, 2015}} Thomas was an outstanding high school basketball player. He was named first-team all-state by the Associated Press as a junior in 2012. He averaged 21.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 2.1 steals in 2012 to lead his team to the Division 2 state championship. Onalaska ended the year with a 27–1 record. Thomas scored 30 points in the state championship game, a 55–38 victory over Kaukauna. His senior year Thomas averaged 28.3 points and 9.7 rebounds, leading his team to the state semifinals and a 24–3 mark, shooting 50.4% percent from the field and 35.8% from beyond the arc. Thomas scored more than 40 points three times, including 41 points in the sectional final and a career-high 50 points in just 2 1/2 quarters vs. Tomah. He participated in the 2013 American Family Insurance High School 3-Point Championship, finishing third. Thomas ended his four-year career as a two-time first-team all-state pick with a 95–12 overall mark and over 2,000 points.{{cite web |title=Matt Thomas - 2016-17 Basketball (M) Roster |url=https://cyclones.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/matt-thomas/8161 |website=cyclones.com |accessdate=February 27, 2020}} An outstanding scorer, Thomas was considered one of the best shooters in the class of 2013 and one of the best players from Wisconsin. A consensus top-100 national recruit, Thomas was ranked No. 51 by ESPN, No. 54 by [[Rivals.com]], and No. 58 by [[Scout.com]] in the final national rankings.{{cite web |last1=Sommerfeldt |first1=Todd |title=Onalaska's Matt Thomas chooses Iowa State |url=http://lacrossetribune.com/sports/onalaska-s-matt-thomas-chooses-iowa-state/article_f77fa370-b671-11e1-9fef-001a4bcf887a.html |website=La Crosse s = 171 | espn schoolid = 66 | rivals overall = 54, 15 (G) | espn overall = 51, 3 (WI), 12 (G) | accessdate = 2015-12-16 | bball = yes }} ==College career== ===Freshman season=== Thomas began his true freshman campaign as a starter for Iowa State. He is only the 20th ISU freshman to start a season opener. He started in the first 15 games before being replaced in the starting line-up by [[Monte Morris]]. Despite becoming the 6th man, Thomas still appeared in all 36 games that season.{{cite web |last1=Hayes |first1=Bennet |title=Fred Hoiberg's Unique Formula Continues To Add Up To Wins |url=http://rushthecourt.net/2013/11/21/fred-hoibergs-unique-formula-continues-to-add-up-to-wins/ |website=rushthecourt.net |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=November 21, 2013}} Over the season Thomas averaged 5.5 points, scored in double figures eight times, and shot 33.6% from behind the arc. He made four three-pointers in a game twice during the season. He made a three in 25 games with 44 three-pointers total, which is good enough for second-most by a Cyclone freshman. ===Sophomore season=== Thomas spent two days in jail following his arrest for an [[Driving under the influence|OWI]] on July 14, 2014.{{cite web |last1=Phillips |first1=Scott |title=Report: Iowa State guard Matt Thomas arrested for OWI, suspended indefinitely |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2014/06/14/report-iowa-state-guard-matt-thomas-arrested-for-owi-suspended-indefinitely/ |website=CollegeBasketballTalk |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=June 14, 2014}} Thomas began his sophomore season serving a three-game suspension.{{cite web |title=Matt Thomas, Abdel Nader suspended |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/11624493/matt-thomas-abdel-nader-iowa-state-cyclones-suspended-3-games |website=ESPN.com |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=October 1, 2014}} Due to increased bench depth his sophomore season, Thomas saw a slightly diminished role. He saw action in 32 total games, scoring in double figures nine times. He was third on the team with 32 three-pointers made. Thomas grabbed a career-high eight rebounds and hit 5–6 shots to score 13 points against Alabama in the season opener.{{cite web |last1=Dible |first1=Max |title=Matt Thomas plays big role in season debut |url=https://www.iowastatedaily.com/sports/mens_basketball/article_5b8857ac-745e-11e4-8ab2-d361cbabedb4.html |website=Iowa State Daily |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=November 24, 2014}} He led the Cyclones in scoring for the first time in his career against Lamar, with 14 points.{{cite web |last1=Murphy |first1=Keith |title=ISU Gets Back To Cyclone Basketball |url=http://whotv.com/2014/12/02/isu-gets-back-to-cyclone-basketball/ |website=whotv.com |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150304144217/http://whotv.com/2014/12/02/isu-gets-back-to-cyclone-basketball/ |archivedate=March 4, 2015 |date=December 3, 2014}} He scored a career-high 17 points at Texas, included 4–6 from the three-point range.{{cite web |title=Niang and Thomas lead No. 14 Iowa State over Texas 85-77 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400585849 |website=ESPN.com |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=February 21, 2015}} ===Junior season=== Due to the season-ending injury of [[Naz Long]], Thomas moved back into the starting lineup.{{cite web |last1=Birch |first1=Tommy |title=Iowa State's Naz Mitrou-Long to miss rest of season |url=http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/basketball-mens/2015/12/15/naz-mitrou-long-iowa-state-cyclones-out-for-season/77380322/ |website=Des Moines Register |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=December 15, 2015}} ==Professional career== ===Obradoiro CAB (2017–2018)=== Thomas played for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] 2017 summer league team. He scored 23 points on 8–9 shooting in the summer league title game to help the Lakers to a 110–98 victory. On August 29, 2017, Thomas signed with [[Obradoiro CAB|Monbus Obradoiro]] of Spain's [[Liga ACB]].{{cite web |title=Matt Thomas: "Me siento muy afortunado de formar parte de esta familia y este club en mi primera experiencia como profesional" |url=http://www.obradoirocab.com/webobra/index.php/es/noticias/2179-matt-thomas-me-siento-muy-afortunado-de-formar-parte-de-esta-familia-y-este-club-en-mi-primera-experiencia-como-profesional |website=Obradoiro CAB - Monbus Obradoiro |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |language=es-ES |date=August 29, 2017}} In his first professional game of his career, Thomas recorded 21 points in 4-for-5 shooting from three-point line as he helped Obradoiro win against Zaragoza.{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Spain/2017/0930_1348_1998.asp|title=Obradoiro 80 - Zaragoza 74|publisher=EuroBasket|date=September 30, 2017|accessdate=March 12, 2020}} ===Valencia (2018–2019)=== On July 11, 2018, Thomas signed a two-year deal with [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]] of Spain's [[Liga ACB]].{{cite web |title=Acuerdo entre Valencia BC y Matt Thomas para las dos próximas temporadas |url=http://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/142076 |website=http |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |language=es-ES |date=July 11, 2018}} He had an effective field goal percentage of 99 percent on catch-and-shoot attempts when unguarded, picking up the nickname Mr. 99%.{{cite web |last1=Rafferty |first1=Scott |title=What Matt Thomas brings to the Toronto Raptors |url=https://ca.nba.com/news/what-matt-thomas-brings-to-the-toronto-raptors/1jv5n9chdr1861i0il5vkaf1d9 |website=NBA.com Canada |url=http://www.raptorscage.ca/justifying-the-hype-around-the-iceman-matt-thomas/ |website=Raptors Cage |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=July 21, 2019}} ===Toronto Raptors (2019–2021)=== On July 19, 2019, Thomas signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web |title=Raptors Sign Matt Thomas |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-release/raptors-sign-matt-thomas |website=NBA.com |accessdate=July 19, 2019 |date=July 19, 2019}} On October 26, 2019, Thomas made his NBA debut, scoring six points and grabbing three rebounds, in the Raptors 108–84 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web |last1=Loung |first1=Steven |title=Raptors' Anunoby shows glimpse of what he could be in rout of Bulls |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/raptors-anunoby-shows-glimpse-rout-bulls/ |website=www.sportsnet.ca |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=October 26, 2019}} On November 25, Thomas suffered a fractured finger on his left hand.{{cite web |title=Raptors' Thomas fractured bone in finger |url=https://www.tsn.ca/toronto-raptors-matt-thomas-fractured-bone-in-finger-1.1403641 |website=TSN |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=November 25, 2019}}{{cite web |title=Raptors' Matt Thomas likely out four weeks with broken finger |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/raptors-matt-thomas-likely-four-weeks-broken-finger/ |website=www.sportsnet.ca |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=November 26, 2019}} He returned to action on January 6, 2020, suiting up on a rehab assignment for the [[Raptors 905]], the Raptors' [[NBA G League]] affiliate.{{cite web |last1=Loung |first1=Steven |title=Rehab stint with 905 helps Matt Thomas shake off rust before Raptors return - Sportsnet.ca |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/g-league-rehab-stint-proves-successful-raptors-matt-thomas/ |website=www.sportsnet.ca |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=January 6, 2020}} On January 7, Thomas returned to the Raptors lineup recording eight points and a career-high six rebounds in the Raptors' 101–99 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web |title=Raptors' Matt Thomas: Sees 15 minutes in return |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/raptors-matt-thomas-sees-15-minutes-in-return/ |website=CBSSports.com |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=January 7, 2020}} On February 8, Thomas scored a career-high 15 points in a 119–118 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |title=Raptors top Nets 119-118, extend record winning streak to 14 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161423 |website=ESPN.com |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=February 8, 2020}} On February 23, Thomas bested his career high with 17 points and five [[3-pointer]]s in a 127–81 victory against the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web |title=Raptors' Matt Thomas: Scores career-high 17 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/raptors-matt-thomas-scores-career-high-17/ |website=CBSSports.com |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=February 23, 2020}}{{cite web |title=Raptors roll to biggest win of season, beat Pacers 127-81 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161485 |website=ESPN.com |accessdate=February 27, 2020 |date=February 23, 2020}} In the Raptors’ sixth game returning from the [[Suspension of the 2019–20 NBA season|suspension of the season]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] on August 10, Thomas scored a career-high 22 points, hitting 4 three-pointers, in a 114–106 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in the [[2020 NBA Bubble|Orlando bubble]].{{cite web |title=Raptors beat Bucks as Boucher, Thomas have career games |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/raptors-beat-bucks-boucher-thomas-career-games/ |website=Sportsnet |publisher=Associated Press |accessdate=11 August 2020}} ===Utah Jazz (2021)=== On March 25, 2021, the Raptors traded Thomas to the [[Utah Jazz]] for a future second-round draft pick.{{cite web |title=Utah Jazz Acquire Matt Thomas |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-acquire-matt-thomas |website=NBA.com |date=March 25, 2021 |accessdate=March 27, 2021}} On April 28, Thomas scored a season-high 17 points on 7-of-7 shooting from the field and 1-of-1 from the three in a 154–105 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{Cite web|title=Jazz's Matt Thomas: Goes off in garbage time|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-matt-thomas-goes-off-in-garbage-time/|access-date=2021-05-02|website=CBSSports.com|date=April 29, 2021 |language=en}} On August 1, he was waived by the Jazz.{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz waive Matt Thomas|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-waive-matt-thomas|date=August 1, 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=August 1, 2021}} ===Chicago Bulls (2021–2022)=== On September 8, 2021, Thomas signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|title=Bulls sign Free Agents|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-free-agents|website=NBA.com|date=September 8, 2021|accessdate=September 8, 2021}} With 13 players out of the lineup due to [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19]] protocols in December, Thomas saw increased playing time. On December 26, he played 19 minutes, scoring five points, in a 113–105 victory over the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite news |title=National Basketball Association |url=https://statsdmz.nba.com/pdfs/20211226/20211226_INDCHI_book.pdf |access-date=28 December 2021 |date=December 26, 2021}} The following day, he made three critical [[Three-point field goal|3-pointers]] in 19 minutes on the floor in a 130–118 victory over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite news |title=National Basketball Association |url=https://statsdmz.nba.com/pdfs/20211227/20211227_CHIATL_book.pdf |access-date=28 December 2021 |date=December 27, 2021}} ===Panathinaikos (2023)=== On January 31, 2023, Thomas made his return to Europe for [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[EuroLeague]], signing a contract through 2024, with the second season being a team option. In 10 EuroLeague games (5 starts), he averaged 8.1 points and 2 rebounds (shooting with 40% from the 3-point line) in 18 minutes per contest. Thomas appeared in only one game in domestic competition due to the Greek league's restrictions on foreign players. On July 15, Panathinaikos opted out of their mutual contract and Thomas became a free agent. ===Alba Berlin (2023–2025)=== On August 7, 2023, Thomas signed a one-year contract with German club [[Alba Berlin]]. The deal reportedly included a buy-out clause for [[EuroLeague]] clubs. ===Granada (2025–2026)=== On August 31, 2025, Thomas signed with [[Fundación CB Granada|Granada]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite web|title=Former Raptors player just found a new job away from the NBA|url=https://raptorsrapture.com/toronto-raptors-matt-thomas-new-job-spanish-club-fundacion-cb-granada-scottie-barnes|access-date=October 29, 2025|website=raptorsrapture.com|language=en}}{{Cite web|title=International Signings: Thomas, Mané, Graham, Robinson|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/08/international-signings-thomas-mane-graham-robinson.html|access-date=October 29, 2025|website=hoopsrumors.com|language=en}} On January 11, 2026, Thomas activated his contract's release clause and left Granada.{{Cite web|title=Matt Thomas hace efectiva su cláusula de salida y deja el Coviran Granada |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/541988-matt-thomas-hace-efectiva-su-clausula-de-salida-y-deja-el-coviran-granada.html|access-date=January 11, 2026|date= January 11, 2026|website=acb.com|language=es}} ===Beşiktaş (2026–present)=== On January 11, 2026, [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş Gain]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|BSL]] and [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] announced Thomas as a new player.{{Cite web|title=Matt Thomas Beşiktaş GAİN’de
